lead: the man who cuts your hair, the tuesday five-a-side, the standing lunch with a woman you no longer like — other people keep a bottom tier of arrangements they can stop attending. no second tier exists in here.
sun: people who meant to ask you for one afternoon find they have entered something. a favour asked over a fence comes back as terms, given level, at the volume of an ordinary sentence, and it is still running when their children are grown. nobody gets a trial period from you. so the street around you is held together by about forty permanent arrangements, and nobody living on it thinks of it as an arrangement.
moon: the entering takes about three seconds and nothing in the three seconds registers size. a wednesday evening and a decade go in through the same slot, at the same weight, and there is no sorting afterwards — the trivial ones did not arrive labelled trivial. so the life accumulates in one direction only, and no running total of what you are inside has ever been available.
pull: there is no minor register. the smallest thing you ever agreed to is kept at the strength of the marriage, and there is no tier below it where a thing could lapse.
tension: something you settled about your own conduct at nineteen, unwitnessed, with nobody on the other end of it, is still in force. release from an undertaking has to come from the other party — you were both parties, and the one who could let you off does not do that. so a boy with no information is still setting terms, and no occasion has come up on which the question could be put.
cost: nothing around you requires maintaining. people who moved abroad still have their arrangement here, intact and unattended, and will find it intact at sixty. the week itself was drawn up by people you would not now recognise — one at twenty-six, one at thirty-four, one at forty-one — each entering something binding on whoever came after, and the one keeping all of it has no standing to convene them.

lead: five of you arrived the same week and agreed something at a table that first winter. two are dead, one went home, and everything here ranks by arrival date — so nobody is left who stands level with you.
sun: an undertaking between equals carries no enforcement. the whole strength of it is that either of you could walk out and neither of you will, and each of you knows the other could. that is what was true at the table that winter. it has been kept to the clause for thirty-one years, with no conversation at any point about whether it still applies.
moon: nobody promoted you. the ones who had been here longer died, and the position closed over you without a vote — a date on a list, checkable, and everyone under it younger in the only way this place counts. so the man you agreed with that winter now waits for you to sit down first, and has done for about a decade, and has said nothing about it.
pull: a promise can only be released by an equal, and seniority has removed every equal you had. so it stands, unreleasable, kept by the one person now too senior to be held to it.
tension: he could say tonight that you are let off and it would not count, because a man who dates his standing from a later week cannot give you anything freely. so the terms run on, kept by the one who no longer has to keep anything, toward the one who can no longer be seen to want them kept. the only two people who were ever party to it are now the two least able to discuss it.
cost: he has kept his side to the letter and so have you, across an inversion of standing that would have ended most arrangements — nothing was ever conditional on who ended up above whom. what has gone is the level. he brings you the good news now and takes the rest elsewhere, and the last unguarded sentence anybody said to you was said at that table, by him.

lead: the founding story gets told at every anniversary and there is a name missing. you found the name in a ledger nobody had opened, in year nine, having already promised the old man you would keep the place going.
sun: he was eighty-one and you were twenty-three and the promise you made him named a duty; it did not name a set of facts the duty depends on. that is the ordinary construction of an undertaking, which is also why no finding of yours has been able to touch it. the terms were settled before the digging started and have not moved a word since.
moon: a cause that explains the thing works here as the next place to start. so the celebrated version went first, then the version underneath it, then the money, and then what happened to the family on the west side in the winter the place was built. all of it landed on somebody with no way out of the building.
pull: you can prove the place should not exist and you will keep it standing until you die. the promise was made to a man who did not know either, and he is dead.
tension: the anniversary comes round and you are the one who speaks, because the promise includes speaking. what you say is true and selected: the year it opened, the men who put the money up, the names on the board. the accurate account is standing behind your shoulder while you do it, and the only two people who would want to hear it are the family it was taken from, and they left the county three generations ago.
cost: very few institutions are ever examined by somebody who has no exit from them, which is why what you know about that place is unusually complete and unusually useless. a person who could resign would have a report to write and somewhere to send it; you have a hall to open on thursdays, a key, and a full account of why it should never have been built.

lead: you stood up in front of about sixty of them the night the works closed and said one thing out loud. the room heard one promise. what actually got made that night was sixty of them, one per person.
sun: a promise fastens onto a person, and a room is not a person. so it divided on the way out of your mouth: each of them left with a whole one, entire and personally theirs, and unconditional. because it was entered rather than announced, no part of it lapsed when the place shut, when they scattered, or when most of them stopped writing.
moon: you knew within a week which of the sixty would ever be in touch again. that faculty runs constantly and reports on the same body twice: this one is on the way back, that one has been leaving for years without saying so. what it has never produced is a shorter list, and the ones you knew would vanish are inside the same sentence as the ones who stayed.
pull: one sentence, sixty people, twenty-two years. all sixty are still individually covered, and the ones who never came back are covered exactly as well as the ones who did.
tension: they get together every couple of years and you are the reason there is anything to get together about, and the warmth in that room runs between them and past you. you hold them one at a time, which is the only way the sentence works — sixty separate live things. so you are at the middle of a body you have never been a member of, being thanked collectively for something that was never given collectively.
cost: a woman you have coffee with and a man who died in another country in the ninth year are covered by the same sentence, at the same weight, and you could not say which of the sixty are still alive. sixty undertakings have run twenty-two years with no register and no reminder, and any one of them would be found intact if it were tested.
